paper.title_en: Spin and Orbital Structure of $f\bar {f}$ in Scalar and Pseudoscalar Decays
paper.abstract_en: We construct the coordinate-space wave function of a fermion-antifermion pair produced in two-body decays of a spin-zero parent. Starting from the S-matrix amplitude we derive a momentum-space wave function and its Fourier transform. For a scalar (${{0}^{ + }}$) coupling we obtain a pure $L = 1$ partial wave whose spin factors select definite orbital projections m for specific spin orientations of f and $\bar {f}$. For a pseudoscalar (${{0}^{ - }}$) coupling the result is a pure $L = 0$ wave with the usual singlet spin structure. We show explicitly why the back-to-back momenta of the final particles do not contradict nonzero orbital angular momentum: $L$ is a property of the relative coordinate. We also discuss why OAM phases are generally invisible in standard HEP measurements that project onto momentum eigenstates, and point to spin-resolved angular correlations as the observable remnants.
